rules.explanation: A graphics proxy or post-processing injector can compete with the DirectX 9 ReShade depth hook.
rules.suggested_action: Preserve all files, use one reviewed proxy chain, and test depth visualization before stereo.

rules.explanation: Camera, skeleton, body and weapon placement can conflict with head-driven view or stereo convergence.
rules.suggested_action: Test locomotion, dialogue, VATS, Pip-Boy, terminals, lockpicking and weapon transitions.

rules.explanation: HUD and menu replacements may require scale, convergence or stereo-depth changes.
rules.suggested_action: Verify readability in both eyes and preserve a desktop fallback profile.

rules.explanation: Native plugins commonly depend on an exact executable and may share hook sites.
rules.suggested_action: Require Fallout3.exe 1.7.0.3 and compare every plugin's supported runtime before launch.

rules.explanation: Rendering changes can alter depth selection, stereo artifacts and performance.
rules.suggested_action: Verify depth, shadows, water, interiors and exterior weather transitions.

rules.explanation: Asset replacement is generally compatible but can exceed VR memory and frame-time budgets.
rules.suggested_action: Measure frame pacing and reduce texture or LOD load when needed.

rules.explanation: Input mods can overlap head-to-mouse, gamepad and recenter bindings.
rules.suggested_action: Check movement, snap/smooth turning, menus, VATS and recenter bindings.

rules.explanation: Alternate launchers and executable patchers affect build identity and FOSE startup.
rules.suggested_action: Re-run executable identification after every patch and never stack patchers blindly.
